half: 1 of 2: even indexes of predicate_pairs.json (52 entries, 45 tables)
readOnly: Every request was a select or explain inside begin ... rollback, through a runner that refuses DDL and DML keywords. Nothing was created, altered or written.
method: Text: for all 52 entries, oldUsing/oldCheck equal the LIVE pg_policies qual/with_check read today, and permissive/cmd/roles match; newUsing/newCheck equal the using/with check text in the migration file 20260927a (parsed from the file); newUsingInline/newCheckInline equal newUsing/newCheck with each helper call replaced by its inline text. All 52 pass.

Real rows: as the default role (postgres, RLS bypassed) inside begin/rollback with request.jwt.claims set for the login, per entry: count(*) filter (where old) vs count(*) filter (where newInline) for USING and CHECK, plus a per-row count where coalesce(old,false) <> coalesce(new,false). Predicates are evaluated once per row in a subquery (offset 0).

Synthetic rows (covers the 4 empty tables and write checks): each table row type built in memory with jsonb_populate_record from {} and 2 real rows, with location_id set to all 13 venues, an unknown uuid and null (text columns also get UPPERCASE, {braced}, leading and trailing space, not-a-uuid and empty string), device_uid/user_id set to the caller, another login and null, menu_board_screens status unpaired/paired, user_locations role owner/manager. Same old vs new comparison.

Helper sets: per login, the four venue sets built from the inline text AND from the migration function bodies pasted verbatim, compared with each other, with the existing pos_accessible_location_keys(), and with pos_can_access(text), pos_can_access(uuid), pos_can_access(uuid::text), ops_can_write and waitlist_can_write called on every venue id, the unknown uuid, null, and the odd text forms. Null is treated as refused on both sides (coalesce), as RLS does.

Negative control: the same harness with a deliberately broken helper (till status active dropped; ops/waitlist active flipped) reports mismatches (closed_checks 147 rows for the Leeds till, cash_movements 16, ops_alerts 5, ops_checklist_tasks 25), so a zero result is not vacuous.

notes: NULL location: pos_can_access returns false, but ops_can_write and waitlist_can_write already return NULL (not false) for a null location whenever the caller has at least one venue (null in a non empty set). The new IN form returns NULL for a null location when the set is non empty and false when it is empty. RLS refuses NULL and false alike (USING hides the row, WITH CHECK rejects it), and policies are only combined with OR/AND, never NOT, so access is the same. The migration header line saying the old functions return false for null is only exactly true for pos_can_access.

The 4 empty tables in this half (floor_table_tombstones x2 entries, waitlist_sms_inbound, wf_user_roles) have no real rows, so their real-row comparison is vacuous; the synthetic rows cover them with both true and false outcomes.

user_locations ul_insert_self_claim WITH CHECK is false for every login and every synthetic row, because can_claim_location needs a venue created_by the caller with no other user_locations rows, and no such venue exists today. The only change in that policy is auth.uid() -> (select auth.uid()); auth.uid() is distinct from (select auth.uid()) was false for all 20 logins, and can_claim_location(location_id) is untouched, so it is identical by construction.

Inner subqueries in td_select, booking_payments paired device read, waitlist_devices_sel and osd_* run under the caller's RLS in production but under postgres here. Old and new differ only in auth.uid() wrapping, so any inner filtering applies equally to both.

Migration helper bodies (accessible_location_ids, accessible_location_uuids with the ids body substituted, ops_writable_location_uuids, waitlist_writable_location_uuids) return exactly the same set as the inline text for all 20 logins, and accessible_location_ids equals the existing pos_accessible_location_keys() for all 20.
sideFindings: closed_checks has two identical indexes: idx_closed_checks_location and idx_closed_checks_location_closed_at, both btree (location_id, closed_at DESC). One can be dropped in a later migration (write cost only).

Live read cost today as the real authenticated role (plain count(*) under current policies): staff_auth_events 485 ms as neil and 454 ms as the Leeds till; closed_checks 493 ms and 414 ms; cash_movements 155 ms and 143 ms. menu_translations and modifier_groups reads are about 1 ms because a cheap read policy answers first, but their write policies pay about 0.7 ms per row (507 ms and 147 ms over the whole table).
